BMI.evidence: Adults with overweight/obesity (BMI between 25 and 35 kg/m2) and with normal fasting plasma glucose levels (3.9 to 5.5 mmol/L) and serum 25(OH)D < 50nmol/L or >50 nmol/L were included in the study.

disease_state.evidence: inferred: Subjects pregnant or breastfeeding, with morbid obesity (BMI > 35 kg/m2), diagnosed with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus, or with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease were excluded from the study.

material_type.evidence: inferred: Two eight-plex serum proteomics experiments were performed for male and female subjects separately, as we have shown previously that vitamin D has sex-specific non-skeletal cardiovascular effects.

sample_source.evidence: For the cross-sectional serum proteomics study, participants were randomly selected from an existing cohort, the Riyadh cohort 2.

sex.value: 4 males with serum 25(OH)D < 50nmol/L; 4 males with serum 25(OH)D > 80 nmol/L; 4 females with serum 25(OH)D < 50nmol/L; 4 females with serum 25(OH)D > 80 nmol/L
sex.evidence: The discovery cohort comprised 16 participants (four males with serum 25(OH)D < 50nmol/L; four males with serum 25(OH)D > 80 nmol/L; four females with serum 25(OH)D < 50nmol/L; four females with serum 25(OH)D > 80 nmol/L).
